Home Is Where the Smart Is

A household tech handbook for the person who looks after a family's devices and accounts.

Type
Page
Edition
1.0
Published
November 12, 2026

Public · v0.1.1

The handbook for a family's unofficial tech lead. Every household has someone everyone calls when the Wi-Fi drops or a strange text arrives. This guide helps them set things up once so the same problems stop coming back. It's open on GitHub.

  • What's in it: twelve chapters covering a map of the household's tech, a family password manager, backups, the router and Wi-Fi, devices and updates, kids' devices, helping aging parents, the smart home, credit freezes and bank alerts, buying and retiring devices, emergencies and digital legacy, and what to do when something goes wrong.
  • Fill-in sheets: a household tech sheet, a device inventory, an emergency card, and an account recovery sheet. None of them holds passwords.
  • Checkups: a yearly checkup, a new device checklist, and a checklist for visiting parents.
  • Licenses: written material under CC BY-SA 4.0, code under MIT, and the names reserved.

Current limits

Credit freeze and reporting steps are for the United States. Settings menus change; the handbook names where to look, and the vendors' own help pages have the latest steps.

Next step

Start with the guides to a password manager for your family and backups you can trust. For hands-on help at home, get in touch.
